In [[number theory]], a '''bi-twin chain''' of length ''k''&nbsp;+&nbsp;1 is a sequence of natural numbers

: <math> n-1,n+1,2n-1,2n+1, \dots, 2^k n - 1, 2^k n + 1 \,</math>

in which every number is [[prime number|prime]].<ref>[[Eric W. Weisstein]], ''CRC Concise Encyclopedia of Mathematics'', CRC Press, 2010, page 249.</ref>

The special case, when the four numbers <math>n-1,n+1,2n-1,2n+1</math> are all primes, they are called '''bi-twin primes''',<ref>[http://www.primenumbers.net/Henri/fr-us/BiTwinRec.htm BiTwin records]</ref> such ''n'' values are

:6, 30, 660, 810, 2130, 2550, 3330, 3390, 5850, 6270, 10530, 33180, 41610, 44130, 53550, 55440, 57330, 63840, 65100, 70380, 70980, 72270, 74100, 74760, 78780, 80670, 81930, 87540, 93240, … {{OEIS|A066388}}

Except 6, all of these numbers are divisible by 30.

The numbers <math>n-1, 2n-1, \dots, 2^kn - 1</math> form a [[Cunningham chain]] of the first kind of length <math>k + 1</math>, while <math>n+1, 2n + 1, \dots, 2^kn + 1</math> forms a Cunningham chain of the second kind. Each of the pairs <math>2^in - 1, 2^in+ 1</math> is a pair of [[twin primes]]. Each of the primes <math>2^in - 1</math> for <math>0 \le i \le k - 1</math> is a [[Sophie Germain prime]] and each of the primes <math>2^in - 1</math> for <math>1 \le i \le k</math> is a [[safe prime]].

== Relation with other properties ==

=== Related chains ===

* [[Cunningham chain]]

=== Related properties of primes/pairs of primes ===

* [[Twin primes]]
* [[Sophie Germain prime]] is a prime <math>p</math> such that <math>2p + 1</math> is also prime.
* [[Safe prime]] is a prime <math>p</math> such that <math>(p-1)/2</math> is also prime.
